newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singtel sees S$1.0 bln capital expenditure FY98.
newsitem.headline: Singtel sees S$1.0 bln capital expenditure FY98.

text.p: Singapore Telecom Ltd expects to spend Singapore $1.0 billion in capital expendiure in financial year 1998, chairman Koh Boon Hwee said on Friday.
"Capital expenditure for FY98 is expected to be in the region of S$1.0 billion," Koh told a news conference after the release of the company's 1996/1997 results.
"The group expects to spend about S$2.5 billion over the next three years," he added.
SingTel's capital expenditure was S$742 million for the year ended March 31, 1997.
Koh said the group would invest the S$1.5 billion the government will pay for the loss of SingTel's monopoly over a period of seven years from 2000.
"The amount will be amortised over a period of seven years to the year 2007. We are looking to reinvest the entire S$1.5 billion received into our core telecommunciations business," Koh said.
Singapore plans to issue one or two licences for basic telecommunications next year for services to be launched in 2000.
SingTel lost its monopolies on the mobile telephone and pager markets on April 1.
